name: Giardia lamblia (giardiasis)
short_description: Binucleate flagellated protozoan (genus Giardia, also called G. duodenalis / G. intestinalis) whose bilaterally symmetric, teardrop-shaped trophozoite (~12-15 x 5-9 um) carries two symmetric anterior nuclei giving it a famously face-like look, a large concave ventral adhesive disc that clamps onto small-intestinal enterocytes, a median body of microtubules, and eight flagella in four bilateral pairs (anterior, posterolateral, ventral, caudal); it does not invade tissue but coats the mucosa, blunts villi and interferes with fat/vitamin absorption, and encysts into an oval four-nucleated environmentally resistant cyst that is shed in faeces and survives in untreated water, making it the classic 'backpacker's/beaver fever' waterborne diarrhoeal parasite.

textbook.1: ✅ PASS (gemini-2.5-flash-image) — CHOSEN. Bilaterally symmetric teardrop/pear body with a broad rounded anterior end tapering to the rear, dorsally domed. Two symmetric lavender nuclei each with a darker karyosome, giving the classic face-like look. A large circular teal ventral disc with clean radiating spiral ridges converging to a central point (no dark hole/aperture — reads as a solid concave sucker, not a mouth). Dusty-rose claw-hammer-shaped median body sits correctly in the rear half, dorsal to the tail flagella. Roughly eight thin flagella emerge in clusters from both sides and trail off the body — close to the required four-pairs/eight-total count though a couple of strands loop near the body making an exact count slightly ambiguous. Muted educational palette, thin crisp outlines, neutral dark charcoal background filling the frame, no text, no border. First attempt passed outright, no re-render needed for this style.

sem.1: ✅ PASS (gemini-2.5-flash-image) — CHOSEN. Photorealistic false-colour SEM plate, single specimen on an even dark background. Warm gold-tan body, two lavender surface bulges reading as the paired nuclei just under the surface, a cooler teal-grey ventral concavity in the correct position (front-facing, not a punched hole) with faint scalloped/spiral texture, and roughly eight thin pale flagella trailing from the base in a natural loose cluster (some looped, as they realistically appear in real SEM plates of this organism — comparable to the real reference micrograph). No text, no border, no cluster of multiple specimens. Honest caveat: the overall silhouette reads more egg/oval than a sharply tapered pear, and because SEM correctly omits interior structures, the median body is not shown (correct for this modality, not a miss).

3d.1: ⚠️ PARTIAL (gemini-2.5-flash-image) — bilaterally symmetric egg/pear body, two correct symmetric nuclei, disc in the right ventral position, but the disc's centre point was rendered as a visible DARK HOLE/slit, reading like an open mouth rather than a solid concave sucker pad. The median body was drawn as a thin curling external tendril (like an extra flagellum) rather than a solid internal bundle. Fix: reword the disc as a uniformly-lit fan/scallop shape with no dark centre, and the median body as a solid shape flush against the body wall.
3d.2: ❌ FAIL (gemini-2.5-flash-image) — the fix-prompt (worded as 'must NOT have a hole/aperture') backfired: the model rendered an even MORE pronounced dark tunnel-like hole at the disc centre, more mouth-like than attempt 1. Median body still a separate external curl. Fix: rewrite the disc description in purely positive terms (scallop-shell / paper-fan, uniformly lit) instead of negating 'hole', since the negative framing seems to have primed the model toward exactly that failure.
3d.3: ✅ PASS (gemini-2.5-flash-image) — CHOSEN. Rewording the disc as a flat fan/scallop-shell patch with fine even radiating ridges and a same-colour (not darker) centre point fixed the false 'mouth' reading entirely: the disc now reads as a clean, uniformly-shaded, solid concave sucker pad. The median body is now a solid dusty-rose comma/hammer shape flush against the body wall beside the flagella base, correctly read as an internal structure rather than a stray appendage. Two symmetric nuclei, natural warm biological tints (not monochrome, not neon), clean dark studio background, eight flagella emerging in two clusters (~4 left, ~4 right). No text, no border. Resolved within the flash tier — no escalation to gemini-3-pro-image needed.

watercolor.1: ⚠️ PARTIAL (gemini-2.5-flash-image) — full-bleed warm aged paper background correctly fills the frame (no sheet/mat/frame), symmetric nuclei and a plausible median body shape, but the ventral disc was painted with a strong dark seam down its centre giving it an unintentional slit/opening appearance. Fix: same disc rewrite as 3d.
watercolor.2: ❌ FAIL (gemini-2.5-flash-image) — same 'do NOT have a hole' negative-framing backfire as 3d attempt 2: the disc centre became an explicit dark oval with a red tongue-like shape inside it, reading unmistakably as an open screaming mouth — the single worst result across the whole set. Fix: purely positive disc description (fan/scallop, evenly lit), no negated 'hole' language.
watercolor.3: ✅ PASS (gemini-2.5-flash-image) — CHOSEN. Same successful positive-framing fix as 3d gen-03: the disc is now a clean fan/scallop shape with fine even ink-line ridges, no dark centre, no mouth-like reading. Median body reads as a solid pink shape flush against the body. Warm cream paper fills the frame edge-to-edge with a soft wash halo directly behind the specimen, no separate sheet/mat/frame. Symmetric nuclei, eight flagella painted as fine trailing ink lines in two loose clusters. No text, no border. Resolved within the flash tier.

reference: ✅ PASS — genuine, single, cleanly-isolated Giardia lamblia trophozoite SEM plate, CDC Public Health Image Library #8698, credit CDC/Janice Haney Carr, public domain ('This image is in the public domain and thus free of any copyright restrictions'). Fetched at its native lores resolution (700x876 px JPEG, 35,495 bytes; a much larger 3.7MB archival TIFF also exists at the same URL pattern but was not opened/used). Viewed directly and confirmed to show exactly what the caption and §1 describe: a clean pear/teardrop-shaped trophozoite with a clearly concave ventral face where the adhesive disc sits, and several long trailing flagella against a plain black background — no other specimens, no clumping. No baked-in text or scale bar was present, so edit_image.py was deliberately skipped per the pipeline rule (a plain deterministic letterboxed resize to 1080x1080 via fetch_reference.py was used instead — nothing was re-illustrated or reshaped). Honest caveat: the image is greyscale (not false-colored) SEM, which is stated plainly rather than dressed up, and because several flagella overlap/loop close to the body it is hard to visually count all eight individually in this single frame even though the four-pairs anatomy is well documented in the literature cited in research.json.
